title: CRISP Tool – SCP Digitalization
summary: A system-driven, integrated digital platform that automates Price Change Calculation (PCR) and Sales, Controlling & Planning (SCP) workflows, bringing transparency, consistency, and governance to contract management.
impact: 100% traceability of price & volume changes | Eliminated Excel-based processes
problem: CMD and SCP processes for price change calculation (PCR) and volume planning were managed through manual, Excel-based workflows. This led to limited end-to-end visibility across Contracts, Plans (TBP/CF), and Actuals, high manual effort and dependency on individual knowledge, inconsistent and non-repeatable PCR and volume calculations, delays in TBP and CF cycles, and limited auditability and explainability of price and volume deviations.
solution: CRISP is a system-driven, integrated digital platform that automates PCR and SCP workflows. It introduces a structured Plan vs Actual explanation framework (Target Cross) to clearly separate and explain price and volume deviations. The platform enables seamless traceability across the value chain: Contracts (Quotation, LOI, PO) → Plan (TBP, CF) → Actuals (YEC, POE billing prices).Currently price change and forecasting happens through this platform for 34 + OE customers

title: DIKE – Document Insights Knowledge Engine
summary: An LLM + RAG-powered knowledge platform that acts as a secure, internal ChatGPT — grounded entirely in Bosch engineering documentation, enabling data democratization and instant access to critical product knowledge.
impact: Data Democratization | Instant knowledge retrieval from internal engineering docs
problem: Engineering teams spend significant time searching for information across servers, SharePoint folders, legacy reports, and multiple repositories. New engineers face steep onboarding curves to understand product history, system behavior, field learnings, and past design decisions. title: AI-Based DRBFM – Sensor Product Engineering
summary: An AI-assisted DRBFM tool trained on Bosch reference documents that enables novice engineers to draft structured risk analyses and expert engineers to validate efficiently — dramatically reducing lead times for 30+ annual design changes in automotive sensor products.
impact: 30+ DRBFMs/year accelerated | L1-grade outputs without 5+ years experience
problem: Bosch supplies automotive sensors (RPM, pressure, temperature, crankshaft) to major OEMs worldwide. These sensors are assembled in inaccessible areas of the vehicle engine bay, and OEMs will not modify their engine layout to accommodate sensor fitment. This forces Bosch to execute frequent design changes, resulting in 30+ DRBFMs annually. Traditionally, conducting a DRBFM requires L1 certification and 5+ years of product-line experience, creating a bottleneck where only a handful of senior engineers can author them. This leads to long lead times, dependency on limited experts, and delays in product development cycles.
solution: An AI-assisted DRBFM platform trained on several Bosch DRBFM reference documents. Using Azure OpenAI GPT-5.2 with embeddings and MongoDB Atlas as a vector database, the system enables novice engineers to draft structured, high-quality DRBFM outputs by retrieving relevant failure modes, design concerns, and countermeasures from historical data. A SerpAPI integration provides external perspectives on design changes, enriching the analysis with industry-wide insights. Expert engineers can then peer-review and validate efficiently, reducing the overall cycle time significantly.

title: AI Requirements Engineering Assistant – Bosch 2WP
summary: A fully deployed AI-powered platform that automates the requirements engineering lifecycle for Bosch Two-Wheeler & Powersports (2WP) — converting unstructured customer inputs into structured, categorized L1 and L2 engineering requirements with gap detection, conflict identification, and full traceability.
impact: Requirement drafting: Hours → Minutes | 50 engineers across 5 product lines
problem: System engineers in the 2WP division manually convert unstructured customer inputs — meeting notes, emails, diagrams, and technical documents — into structured engineering requirements across L1 (high-level) and L2 (detailed) stages. This process is time-consuming, error-prone, and heavily dependent on individual expert knowledge. Engineers struggle with identifying gaps, missing information, and conflicts across requirement categories such as CAN Messages, Diagnostics, Monitoring, Fault Implementation, Hardware Tolerances, Software Implementations, and Calibration. With multiple product lines (ABS/Safety, Engine Management, Electric Powertrain, Connectivity, Vehicle Computer), maintaining consistency and traceability across teams is a significant challenge.
solution: A fully deployed AI-powered requirements engineering assistant that automates the entire L1-to-L2 lifecycle. Engineers upload documents (PDF, Excel, Word) and images (diagrams, whiteboard photos), and the AI generates structured, categorized L1 requirements automatically. It identifies missing information, assumptions, and gaps. After engineer review, the system generates detailed L2 requirements with test approaches, conflict detection against existing system specifications, and safety/cyber linkage. The platform includes DOORS integration for existing requirements, session history for saving and resuming work, Word document export, web search for datasheets and technical references, and an admin panel with usage analytics. Deployed on-premises within Bosch infrastructure with Azure AD SSO and SC2 data classification.

title: FTA & CTH Classification using GenAI
summary: A GenAI-powered customs classification tool that automates CTH (Customs Tariff Heading) identification and FTA (Free Trade Agreement) applicability analysis — returning the nearest 3 matching HSN codes with duty rates, eliminating manual errors across 98 CBIC chapters, and enabling proactive FTA savings for Bosch India imports.
impact: 50% reduction in penalties & bad cost | FTE reduction from 6 to 3 annually | Proactive FTA savings
problem: Determining basic customs duty for imported parts/components in India involves a manual, error-prone process. The foreign trade and taxation teams at Bosch manually navigate the government CBIC portal, sifting through 98 chapter IDs to ascertain the correct CTH code and customs duty rates based on product type, make, and end use. Selecting an incorrect HSN code has two costly outcomes: if the chosen rate is lower than actual, Bosch receives customs notices for underpayment; if higher, Bosch incurs direct financial loss from overpayment. Additionally, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) between India and countries of origin offer concessional duty rates, but neglecting to identify and apply applicable FTAs results in further direct losses — Bosch pays more customs duty than necessary. The entire process depends heavily on SME knowledge, lacks standardization, and carries significant compliance and financial risk.
solution: A GenAI-powered customs classification tool that comprehensively scans all 98 CBIC chapters and FTA notifications released by the Indian government. For indirect materials, users input product description, usage, material type, and dismantled status, and the tool returns the nearest 3 matching HSN codes along with corresponding BCD (Basic Customs Duty) and IGST rates. For FTA identification, the tool takes HSN and country of origin to surface applicable Free Trade Agreements with concessional duty rates and notification numbers. Built on Azure OpenAI GPT-5.2 with embeddings and MongoDB Atlas as a vector database, the system uses natural language search over the Custom Tariff dataset. A bulk update module enables the foreign trade team to batch-process FTA applicability, savings, and notification numbers across multiple parts. Change history tracking ensures full auditability of CTH, BCD, FTA, and IGST modifications. The project runs in 2 phases: Phase 1 (FTA) and Phase 2 (CTH).

title: PROP-EL – Prohibition of Parts – End of Life
summary: A big data-driven dashboard and analytics solution that identifies non-moving and prohibition-eligible parts across 50,000+ part numbers and 820 suppliers — enabling transparent prohibition alignment between M/PU, BU, rBU, and MA, and supporting a 33–37% purchase volume reduction through elimination of unutilized part numbers.
impact: 33–37% PV reduction | ~6,900 unutilized PNs identified | 194 MEUR purchase volume transparency
problem: Bosch’s purchasing organization manages ~50,000 part numbers across 820 suppliers with a purchase volume of 194 MEUR, but only 30% (~15,330) of these part numbers are active. Supply chain planning and price planning year-on-year are complicated by this large volume of dormant parts. For CONV (conventional powertrain) alone, the dataset includes 180,000 line items. Proposing prohibition is challenging because pump-level prohibition differs from component-level prohibition, and alignment with BU prohibition strategy and delivery obligations adds complexity. Non-moving and exotic parts create firefighting situations, and supplier insolvencies or exits — common in CONV — amplify cost risks for parts that may no longer be needed.
solution: A big data approach for data collation and analysis across 6 years of purchasing data (2018–2023) from PS consolidation onwards, covering IP, NHA, VE, UP, and UIN categories across JP, IN, DE, BR, and TH locations. The PROP-EL dashboard provides interactive analytics with multiple selection criteria, part number search functionality, Plan vs Actual comparisons for quantity and purchase volume, and annual trend distributions. The pilot at CONV @ RBJP identified ~300 unique PNs with planned quantities but zero deliveries, and ~6,600 unique PNs with zero planned quantity and zero deliveries — all representing unrealized purchase volume affecting PUR performance. Findings were shared with JP purchasing management, stakeholders, PS-AB, and MA to jointly define a roadmap for inclusion into the prohibition campaign.

title: AI-Based Variant Optimizer – Camshaft Rationalization
summary: An AI agent that compares 1,500+ camshaft variant drawings against master specifications to identify rationalizable part numbers — achieving 20–22% part number reduction across 200+ components, streamlining the supply chain and reducing costs for diesel inline pump production.
impact: 12M INR annual recurring savings | 20–22% part numbers rationalized | 200+ components analyzed
problem: Bosch had accumulated over 1,500 variants of camshafts for the diesel inline pump, primarily due to design indiscipline — the design team released new drawings with unique part numbers for every customer demand, even when specifications were identical or nearly identical to existing parts. The organization estimated that at least 30% of camshafts shared the same specifications but carried different part numbers. This variant explosion made supply chain management inefficient, increased inventory complexity, and drove up costs through unnecessary tooling, procurement, and logistics for duplicate parts.
solution: Built an AI agent that systematically compares all offer drawings against the master drawing to identify rationalizable part numbers. The Streamlit-based front end, hosted on Azure with AI Search, allows designers to upload a master drawing and key in basic dimensions. The agent then crawls across all part numbers in the system, extracts and compares dimensions from engineering drawings, and identifies part numbers with matching or equivalent specifications that can be consolidated. Results are loaded into Excel for review and rationalization decisions. Executed as a one-time, mission-mode activity across 200+ components.

summary: An AI-powered web platform for throttle-valve actuator quotations (DV-E / RKL-E) that automates Bill of Materials generation with pricing, converts multi-format customer RFQ documents into structured Excel with 99.8%+ completeness, and provides a Bosch knowledge base for semantic evaluation of requirements — deployed on Azure Static Web Apps with GitHub CI/CD.
impact: RFQ processing: Hours → Minutes | 99.8%+ extraction completeness | 34 customer formats supported
problem: The throttle-valve actuator quotation process (DV-E / RKL-E) involved significant manual effort across multiple stages. Generating Bills of Materials required engineers to manually select components, apply pricing rules, and handle currency conversions. Customer RFQ documents arrived in widely varying formats — from VW Lastenheft to Ford specifications — across 34 different customers, each with unique layouts, tables, charts, and sometimes German-language content. Converting these into structured, comparable Excel formats was time-consuming, error-prone, and required per-customer setup. Additionally, evaluating RFQ requirements against Bosch's own product specifications and standards required engineers to manually search through internal PDFs, with no systematic way to assess compliance or identify gaps across requirement rows.
solution: A comprehensive AI-powered web platform deployed on Azure Static Web Apps with GitHub CI/CD (v0.21.1) that addresses the full quotation lifecycle through three integrated modules. The BoM Generator enables family and diameter selection with automatic bill of materials construction from fixed rules, configurable component inclusion/exclusion, INR pricing with real-time currency conversion, Bosch-branded Excel export, and full generation history. The RFQ-to-Excel module reads customer requirement PDFs in any format across 34 customers without per-customer setup — extracting sections, tables, and charts as images, translating German to English, adding page number references, and achieving 99.8%+ field completeness. The Bosch Knowledge Base & Evaluation module allows users to upload Bosch PDFs, perform semantic and keyword search, and generate verdicts per RFQ row with source citations for compliance assessment.

title: DBC → Requirements Document Generator
summary: A web application that converts customer DBC files into draft CAN requirement specifications in the Bosch Word template — reducing document preparation from ~10 days to ~2 days (~80% effort reduction) with built-in DBC quality checks and consistent, error-free output.
impact: ~80% effort reduction per document | 10 days → 2 days | Built-in DBC quality checks
problem: Some OEMs send their CAN communication requirements only as a DBC file, with no requirements document. Before development can start, a Bosch 2WP engineer has to read every message and signal and write the CAN requirement specification by hand. For one vehicle network that takes about 10 working days. The work is repetitive and easy to get wrong: bit positions, ranges, default and invalid values are all copied by hand, leading to errors that propagate into development.
solution: A web application that turns the customer DBC into a draft CAN requirement specification in the Bosch Word template. The engineer uploads the DBC file in the browser, chooses the ECU(s) to document (e.g. ABS, or all ECUs), marks messages as same-as-general-spec or not-requested where needed, and downloads the Word document. For each ECU the document is split into Transmit and Receive messages and signals. For every message it lists the transmitter, receivers, periodicity and DLC. For every signal it lists unit, range, resolution, invalid values, byte/bit layout, default value and value tables. The table of contents, header, footer and cover page are filled in automatically. The tool also performs a DBC quality check — listing problems such as overlapping signals, ranges that don't fit the bit length, missing units and missing receivers — which can be raised with the OEM early.
users: Bosch 2WP Engineers, System Engineers, CAN Communication Teams
results: Draft preparation reduced from ~10 days to ~2 days — roughly 80% less effort per document

Consistent output: every document follows the same Bosch template and structure, regardless of who generates it
Faster start of development: requirements are ready for review within days of receiving the DBC
Customer DBC files processed in memory and never stored, ensuring data security

title: Agentic AI Customer Intelligence Platform
summary: An agentic AI platform that ingests and classifies stakeholder emails from SQW (field quality) and Sales teams across 3 OEMs (Tata, MSIL, M&M), scoring each thread on 8 polarity dimensions to give C-suite leaders a real-time, citation-backed intelligence briefing — replacing reactive, post-mortem analysis with early-warning alerts and a centralized, searchable knowledge base per OEM.
impact: 3 OEMs onboarded | 309 threads scored | 8 scoring dimensions | PoC → Production transition
problem: Bosch management visiting OEM customers had no structured way to prepare on current burning issues. Customer intelligence was scattered across individual email threads in SQW (field complaints / downstream quality) and Sales (upstream topics like acquisitions, commercial negotiations) teams. Issues surfaced only after escalation, subtle sentiment shifts went unnoticed for months, communication knowledge was tribal and fragmented across reps, and there was no shared analytical framework — leading to inconsistent, post-mortem analysis rather than proactive relationship management.
solution: An agentic AI platform that productionizes stakeholder-email data pipelines from PoC to production. Email data is collected via two pipelines: a one-time Power Automate backfill of 6 months of legacy mailbox history (since Jan 2025) to seed the knowledge base, and a daily scheduled bot (Power Automate, 11:30 PM) that auto-routes emails from specified customer domains through Outlook folders → OneDrive → Azure Blob (month-wise Excel files) → the platform. The platform ingests and classifies email threads, scoring each on 8 polarity dimensions across Quality and Sales contexts. Three views are provided: a Dashboard with OEM-level score snapshots and confidence ratings, a Portfolio view for strategic customer briefings (Tata, MSIL, M&M), and an Ask Engine for citation-backed Q&A with confidence scoring. The platform enables C-suite leaders to walk into OEM meetings fully prepared on current issues, sentiment trends, and relationship health.
